chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The house and the slave girl are not sold to settle debts, and that is because the man must have a shelter to dwell in and a servant to serve him.

key_terms.الْجَارِيَةُ: The slave girl or female servant

ai.seo_question: What assets are exempt from being sold to pay off debts in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the principle of preserving the debtor's essential means of subsistence (istighna) by exempting their primary residence and female slave from forced sale to satisfy debts. Rooted in the practical necessity of human dignity and daily living, this ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on preventing destitution while balancing creditor rights. It underscores the ethical dimension of debt collection in Islamic law, ensuring that enforcement does not strip the individual of their basic social and domestic stability.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Neither sell the house nor the slave girl regarding the debts, and that is because it is a must for the man a shelter which he can dwell in, and a servant who serves him’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Halabiy who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
a servant and a house must not be sold; it is necessary for a man to have a shelter and a servant.”
